title: Introduction to Database Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of introduction to database integration in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Why ASP applications use databases and Relational database fundamentals.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study introduction to database integration as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 65 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to Database Integration matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP applications commonly use ADO to access relational databases through a provider. For 'Introduction to Database Integration', validate inputs, prefer `ADODB.Command` parameters for values, close Recordsets and Connections, and handle failures without exposing the query, connection string, or database details. Parameter syntax, supported types, cursor behavior, and connection string details can vary by provider; verify them against the installed driver and database.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Why ASP applications use databases; Relational database fundamentals; Tables, rows, and columns; Primary and foreign keys; SQL queries and CRUD operations; The role of database providers. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use synthetic records in a local test database and a least-privilege database account. Record the database/provider version and verify both success and failure cases. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of introduction to database integration. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of introduction to database integration using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Why ASP applications use databases. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
